text:
kevin: Hey everyone, first day! Pulled the repo and ran `docker compose up` from Windows PowerShell. web keeps failing to connect to Postgres with `could not connect to server: Connection refused`. postgres container starts then exits with permission errors. Any quick tips?

Olga: Welcome! :wave: Common culprits on Windows: host-mounted folders with Windows ACLs, mixing WSL vs Windows docker contexts, or accidentally binding host port 5432 when host Postgres is already running. Can you paste the postgres service from your compose?

kevin: Sure, it's small:

kevin: ```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
  web:
    build: .
    depends_on:
      - postgres
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:example@postgres:5432/myapp_dev
```

Ravi (infra): A few things to check in order: 1) Are you running `docker compose` from WSL or PowerShell? Running from PowerShell will mount a Windows path into the container and you can get permission issues. 2) If you have a local host postgres, the `ports: - "5432:5432"` will fail to bind. 3) If the volume was created by root (maybe from using sudo earlier), Postgres won't be able to write.

kevin: I'm in PowerShell atm. Logs show `FATAL: could not open directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Permission denied`. I tried `sudo` with Docker earlier which probably created the dir as root.

Olga: That matches. Two quick fixes: A) switch to running from WSL in your repo folder (recommended), or B) change to an anonymous volume `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` so Docker manages it. To fix the existing host folder permissions: `icacls` on Windows is messy; easiest is to delete `./pgdata` and recreate from WSL or use a Docker-managed volume.

kevin: Switched to WSL and re-ran without host port mapping (removed ports). Postgres still reported `database "myapp_dev" does not exist` then the web timed out connecting initially.

Ravi (infra): Remember `depends_on` doesn't wait for DB readiness. Add a healthcheck for postgres or have the web entrypoint wait for `pg_isready`. Example quick entrypoint wrapper: `sh -c "until pg_isready -h postgres -p 5432; do sleep 1; done; exec npm start"`. Also ensure your web uses `postgres` hostname not `localhost` when in a container.

kevin: Added wait loop and healthcheck. Now pg_isready works but web was still failing to connect to Redis with `Connection refused`. I had REDIS_HOST=localhost in my .env.

Olga: Yup that will do it. When the app runs in a container, service DNS names are the right hostnames. Set REDIS_HOST=redis (or redis:6379 in the URL). Also verify no `network_mode: host` in compose  that breaks cross-container DNS.

kevin: Changed REDIS_HOST and removed `ports:` mapping. Everything boots fine locally now. Thanks! :tada:

Ravi (infra): Nice. Small onboarding checklist suggestion: 1) run `docker compose` from WSL if on Windows, 2) prefer Docker-managed volumes on Windows to avoid ACL issues, 3) avoid `ports:` for internal-only services, 4) add healthchecks or wait-for logic for DB init, and 5) use service hostnames for inter-service comms.

devbot: Action: please add a tiny PR to update onboarding README with Windows/WSL volume and networking tips + a sample healthcheck for Postgres. :memo:
